title: Enhancing the resilience of the gilt repo market – discussion paper feedback statement
summary: The Bank of England has published a feedback statement summarising industry responses to its September 2025 discussion paper on enhancing gilt repo market resilience. While respondents broadly supported the objective, they raised significant concerns about the proportionality of proposed mandatory reforms including central clearing mandates and non-risk-sensitive minimum haircuts. The Bank indicated it will continue exploring policy design options that enhance liquidity supply in stress while working to overcome identified barriers to greater central clearing adoption.
key_points: Bank and FPC consider gilt repo market resilience a central priority following stress episodes in March 2020 and September 2022 LDI crisis
Market structure has shifted: multinational leveraged hedge funds have increased participation while pension funds have become less active
Industry respondents broadly supported the resilience objective but opposed mandatory central clearing, citing access barriers, operational constraints, and cost considerations
Most respondents raised concerns about non-risk-sensitive minimum haircuts, noting these would raise funding costs and potentially divert activity to other markets
Respondents proposed alternative incentives for voluntary clearing adoption: cross-product margining, expanded collateral pools, and inclusion of Bank's STR facility in clearing
The Bank intends to explore market structure changes enabling greater central clearing adoption and improve risk management practices and margin frameworks
why_it_matters: The gilt repo market is critical infrastructure for UK financial stability, government cash management, and market-based funding. This feedback statement indicates the Bank is exploring potential reforms including central clearing mandates and minimum haircuts, though no firm commitments are made. Market participants should monitor this policy development as outcomes could affect clearing requirements, margin practices, and dealer balance sheet management in the UK gilt market.
market_structure_context: The document discusses structural reforms to the gilt repo market including potential central clearing mandates and minimum haircuts, addressing market dynamics and liquidity provision in stress scenarios. Key market structure concerns include dealer balance sheet constraints, tri-party repo development, and CCP margin procyclicality.
